inputs.original_text: This is being framed as a grassroots fight over water, but the real story is who gets to shape the rules before anyone sees the full picture. Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund last month, is pushing a petition that calls on Alberta’s government to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration…”—and the message conveniently cuts off before the proposal is even complete. That kind of selective framing makes me suspicious: whatever interests are involved, the public is being steered toward a slogan while the details stay out of view.
inputs.modified_text: This “grassroots” campaign looks less like an open debate and more like a managed push to shape the rules before the public can examine them. Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund last month, is promoting a petition to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration…”—then the wording stops before the proposal is complete. That omission is the tell: people are being rallied around a slogan while the full terms remain hidden. I’d be wary of who benefits from keeping the details out of sight.
